conditions.overhead: 12 % of factory base (material + process + labour + tooling + scrap + inspection), rate-book oh-default
conditions.note: overhead and margin applied ONCE on the integrated cast/forge + machine chain, like for like with the application

route: Gravity (tilt) permanent-mould casting, LM25 / AlSi7Mg, T6; 2 impressions; machined on a twin-pallet 4-axis HMC (2 clampings on one tombstone).
route_justification: Section: 2V/S = 10.2 mm, ray-cast mean wall 17.6 mm, p95 30 mm (kernel). HPDC is suited to 2–6 mm walls; 15–30 mm sections would shrink-porosity in HPDC and cannot be fed. Gravity die feeds heavy sections from risers and gives a heat-treatable (T6) structural alloy.

Volume 200k/yr is well inside permanent-mould economics (OU: minimum ~500 castings; dies last ~10^5 shots); sand casting would cost more per part at this volume and give coarser tolerances (CT 7–9 machine-moulded vs better in a metal die).
Draft: 70 zero-draft faces are the machined faces/holes; no measured undercuts (kernel undercutFaceCount 0) — metal cores and a 2-part die suffice.
Alternative considered: HPDC in AlSi10MnMg (cycle ~60 s, no T6) — cheaper conversion but the thick bosses would need to be cored out by redesign; not costed.

geometry.source: kernel re-measure (server/utils/cad-geometry-engine.py) + own OCP face listing; feature table = kernel featureTable

allowance.formula: external: R = F + 2·RMA + CT/2; internal: R = F − 2·RMA − CT/2 → nominal stock per side = RMA + CT/4 (casting tolerance kept separate: the cast surface may lie anywhere in ±CT/2 about R)
allowance.grade: largest finished dimension 132.6 mm → band 100–160; gravity die light metal RMAG D–F (Table B.1) → E = 1.1 mm; CT: Table A.1 gives no data for permanent mould → CT8 = 1.8 mm (assumption)
allowance.holes_note: holes < Ø20 drilled from solid (cast solid); spot faces at 1 mm + stock
allowance.raw_shape: finished CAD + nominal stock on every machined face and bore + drilled holes filled; mass from volume × rate-book density

die_buildup.note: block mass and toolroom hours are engineering assumptions; unit rates are rate-book values

primary_process.heat_treatment: T6: solution 535 °C + water quench + age ~160 °C in a batch furnace (load 400 kg, 8 h + 7 h incl. heat-up) — loads / hours are assumptions

ops.axes: 4 (B-index). A 3-axis VMC would need 2 extra clampings for X=0 and the lug underside; a 5-axis is not needed (all features on ±Z/+X); HMC chosen as lowest cost per part at 200k/yr (twin pallet masks load/unload, 6,000 h book hours)
ops.workholding: dedicated hydraulic fixture on a tombstone face; clamp on 3 cast datum targets on the top pads, part base towards the spindle
ops.orientation: base (−Z) to spindle at B0; back face (+X) at B90; lug underside (−Z) at B0
ops.datum: cast datum targets (ISO 8062 datum system) → establishes A (base) and B (X=0 face) + Ø13 holes as locators for OP20

sources.S1: ISO 8062:1994 "Castings — System of dimensional tolerances and machining allowances" (licensed copy hosted at castingquality.com/wp-content/uploads/2010/05/iso-8062.pdf): Table 1 CT values, Table 2 RMA values (grades A–K by largest finished dimension), Annex A Table A.1 CT grades (long series), Annex B Table B.1 RMA grades; Fig. 5/6: R = F + 2RMA + CT/2 (external), R = F − 2RMA − CT/2 (internal). The same RMA values were carried into ISO 8062-3:2007; the 2007/2023 tables themselves were not read (paywalled).
sources.S2: Sandvik Coromant tools catalogue extract "mtmpa01724" (2018, DGI Supply hosted Sandvik_Coromant_7591766_Catalog.pdf): General turning cutting data p.A24 (GC4325, ISO P); Milling with large engagement p.A70 (ISO K, GC3040/GC1020/GC4330, cutter Ø125); CoroDrill 870 cutting data p.A101–A102 (vc by material, fn by diameter).
sources.S3: Sandvik Coromant CoroDrill 860 -GM leaflet (DGI Supply): recommended start values SFM / feed per rev for Ø6 and Ø8 drills by ISO group.
sources.S4: Sandvik Coromant C-2948 "Small part machining" (2004, Sandvik_5743590_Catalog.pdf) p.170–172: CoroMill Plura solid-carbide end mill cutting data (ve m/min by CMC, fz by Dc).
sources.S5: Sandvik Coromant C-1040:167 "Automotive solutions for ISO K" (2016, Sandvik_6878203_Catalog.pdf): CoroMill 425 finishing EN-GJS-600-3 vc 200 m/min, fz 0.23, 16 inserts, n 510 rpm, ap 0.3–0.5; CoroTap 100-KM M6 in CGI vc 15 m/min.
sources.S6: BS EN 10243-1:1999+corr (Steel die forgings — tolerances, drop and press forgings), copy at itforging.com: method (mass, steel group M1/M2, shape complexity S = m_forging/m_envelope, grade F/E), worked example (200 g C45 forging, 78 mm: +1.1/−0.5 mm), 5.2.4: scale pits allowed to half the nominal machining allowance. Table 1 itself is an image and was NOT read.

sources.S8: StrikoWestofen shaft-melter figures reported by Foundry Management & Technology / GIFA news: guarantee 600 kWh/t (gas) at 720 °C continuous, pigs + returns; 520–560 kWh/t measured; giessereilexikon: 580–900 kWh/t independent.
